= Couchbase Capella Release Notes
:page-component-name: cloud
:page-capella-type: Operational

== October 2026 Changelog

* Expanded AWS and Azure region availability
+
Couchbase Capella nows supports 2 new regions:
+
--
* AWS
** Asia Pacific (Osaka) -- `ap-northeast-3`
* Azure
** Italy North (Milan) -- `italynorth`
--

* New Organization Roles
+
Capella adds 3 new organization-level roles:

** xref:organizations:organization-user-roles.adoc#organization-billing-administrator[`Organization Billing Administrator`]: full access to *Billing*. 
They can view billing and usage, manage payment methods, set up billing alerts, and create and view Billing support tickets. 
They have no access to clusters, projects, or data.

** xref:organizations:organization-user-roles.adoc#organization-billing-viewer[`Organization Billing Viewer`]: read-only access to *Billing* and *Support*. 
They can view billing, usage reports, billing alerts, and Billing support tickets. 
They cannot manage payment methods or create alerts.

** xref:organizations:organization-user-roles.adoc#organization-read-only[`Organization Read-Only Member`]: read-only access to the organization's settings, users and projects, with no need for project membership.
It does not give access to cluster data or billing.

+
These roles let you give users access to billing or organization-wide visibility without making them an xref:organizations:organization-user-roles.adoc#organization-role-organization-owner[`Organization Owner`] or adding them to projects.

== September 2026 Changelog

* Increased node limits for GCP and Azure operational clusters
+
Couchbase Capella now supports scaling operational clusters on GCP and Azure beyond the previous 27-node limit up to 50 nodes. 
Higher node counts can also be accommodated based on your workload requirements. 
+
To raise the node limit for your organization, open a xref:support:manage-support.adoc#create-support-ticket[Support Ticket] with Couchbase Capella Support.

* Couchbase Server 8.0.3
+
Creating a new operational cluster with Couchbase Server 8.0 now deploys the Couchbase Server 8.0.3 maintenance release.
This version includes bug fixes.
+
For more information about this version of Couchbase Server, see xref:8.0@server:release-notes:relnotes.adoc#release-8-0-3[Couchbase Server 8.0.3].

== August 2026 Changelog

* XDCR Conflict Logging
+
Capella now supports conflict logging for replications between operational clusters running Couchbase Server 8.0 or later.
You can enable conflict logging when you xref:clusters:xdcr/manage-xdcr-replications.adoc#between-capella-dbs[create] or xref:clusters:xdcr/manage-xdcr-replications.adoc#modify-replication[modify] a replication.
+
For more information, see xref:clusters:xdcr/xdcr.adoc#conflict-logging[Conflict Logging].

* Couchbase Server 7.6.12
+
Creating a new operational cluster with Couchbase Server 7.6 now deploys the Couchbase Server 7.6.12 maintenance release.
This version includes bug fixes.
+
For more information about this version of Couchbase Server, see xref:7.6@server:release-notes:relnotes.adoc#release-7612[Couchbase Server 7.6.12].

== June 2026 Changelog

* Couchbase Server 8.0.2
+
Creating a new operational cluster with Couchbase Server 8.0 now deploys the Couchbase Server 8.0.2 maintenance release.
This version includes bug fixes.
+
For more information about this version of Couchbase Server, see xref:8.0@server:release-notes:relnotes.adoc#release-802[Couchbase Server 8.0.2].

* Slack and Microsoft Teams Integrations for Alerts
+
Capella now supports native alert integrations for Slack and Microsoft Teams.
You can send cluster and App Service xref:reference:alert-reference.adoc#metric-alerts[metric-based alerts] directly to your team's preferred Slack or Microsoft Teams channels by using the Capella UI or the Management REST API.
+
Customize alert payloads with either standard or advanced templates for Slack and Microsoft Teams integrations.
To configure an alert integration, see xref:clusters:monitoring/configure-slack-integration.adoc[]
and xref:clusters:monitoring/configure-microsoft-integration.adoc[].
+
For more information about alert integrations, see xref:clusters:monitoring/alert-integration.adoc[].

== May 2026 Changelog 

* Capella iQ Expands with AWS Bedrock Support
+
Capella iQ now leverages multiple AI model providers to power its AI-assisted capabilities, delivering flexibility, improved reliability, and greater scalability.
Support for AWS Bedrock-hosted models enables a more robust and performant experience across query generation and insights.
+
This enhancement is fully managed and requires no changes to your existing workflows.
+
For more information about model usage and configuration, see xref:get-started:capella-iq/work-with-capellaiq.adoc#model-provider[Work Faster with Capella IQ].

* XDCR for Multi-Node Clusters Over Private Link on Azure
+
Couchbase Capella's support for XDCR through private endpoint connectivity is now extended to clusters hosted on Azure.
Replicate data between clusters entirely over a private network connection without exposing traffic to the public Internet.
+
This feature is currently only available upon request from xref:support:manage-support.adoc#create-support-ticket[Couchbase Capella Support].
+
For more information, see xref:clusters:xdcr/manage-xdcr-security.adoc#private-endpoints[Replicate Data Across a Private Endpoint Connection].

* Prometheus for Multi-Node Clusters Over Private Link on Azure
+
Couchbase Capella's native support for scraping Prometheus metrics endpoints through private endpoint connectivity is now extended to clusters hosted on Azure.
This capability allows you to collect observability data from your internal resources without exposing endpoints to the public Internet.
+
This feature is currently only available upon request from xref:support:manage-support.adoc#create-support-ticket[Couchbase Capella Support].
+
For more information, see xref:clusters:monitoring/prometheus.adoc[].

== March 2026 Changelog

* Default Billing Alerts and Low Credit Warnings for Prepaid Accounts
+
If you use pre-paid credits to pay for your usage in Capella, Capella now creates default billing alerts automatically when new pre-paid credits are applied to your account.
+
When you xref:clusters:create-database.adoc[create a new cluster] or xref:billing:change-support-plan[change a cluster's Support Plan] and your pre-paid credit balance is depleted or running low, Capella also shows warnings to help you avoid unexpected xref:billing:billing.adoc#pay-as-you-go-credits[pay-as-you-go charges] and choose the right Support Plan with confidence.
+
For more information, see xref:billing:about-billing-alerts.adoc#default-billing-alerts[Default Billing Alerts] and xref:billing:billing.adoc#low-credits[Low Credit Warning Calculations].

== February 2026 Changelog

* Couchbase Server 7.6.10
+
Creating a new operational cluster with Couchbase Server 7.6 now deploys the Couchbase Server 7.6.10 maintenance release.
This version includes bug fixes.
+
For more information about this version of Couchbase Server, see xref:7.6@server:release-notes:relnotes.adoc#release-7610[Couchbase Server 7.6.10].

* Custom Subdomains in Capella Endpoints
+
You can now customize endpoints for Capella resources, such as URLs for clusters, private links, and nodes, with unique identifiers.
This option is now also available for GCP and Azure clusters through the xref:management-api-reference:index.adoc#tag/Organizations/operation/putOrganizationConfiguration[Capella Management API].
+
This feature is currently only available upon request from xref:support:manage-support.adoc#create-support-ticket[Couchbase Capella Support].

* Couchbase Capella Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) for Azure now supports unique Entra ID applications per Capella project and is now generally available.
+
You can now configure specific Azure Key Vault connections for each project individually, rather than relying on a single Entra ID application across your entire organization.
+
For more information, see xref:security:cmek.adoc[].

* Capella operational clusters now support fine-grained RBAC for cluster access credentials
+
You can now define fine-grained Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) for cluster access using advanced access credentials.
Advanced access credentials allow you to assign combinations of fine-grained privileges and roles to cluster access credentials at the bucket, scope, and collection levels.
+
Basic access credentials that assign read, write, or read/write access at the bucket, scope, and collection level are still available.
+
For more information about advanced access credentials, see xref:clusters:cluster-rbac.adoc[].

* XDCR for Multi-Node Clusters Over Private Link
+
Couchbase Capella has enhanced the security of your multi-cluster topology.
Capella can now support XDCR through private endpoint connectivity, allowing you to replicate data between clusters entirely over a private network connection.
+
This feature is currently only available upon request from xref:support:manage-support.adoc#create-support-ticket[Couchbase Capella Support].
+
For more information, see xref:clusters:xdcr/manage-xdcr-security.adoc#private-endpoints[Replicate Data Across a Private Endpoint Connection].

* Prometheus for Multi-Node Clusters Over Private Link
+
Couchbase Capella is announcing native support for scraping Prometheus metrics endpoints through private endpoint connectivity.
This capability allows you to collect observability data from your internal resources without exposing endpoints to the public Internet.
+
This feature is currently only available upon request from xref:support:manage-support.adoc#create-support-ticket[Couchbase Capella Support].
+ 
For more information, see xref:clusters:monitoring/prometheus.adoc[].

== December 2025 Changelog

* Couchbase Capella now supports Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) for clusters running in Microsoft Azure.
With CMEK, you can use your own keys stored in Azure Key Vault to protect data-at-rest, giving you tighter control over your encryption lifecycle and compliance.
+
This feature is currently only available upon request.
For more information, see xref:security:cmek.adoc[].
